name: The Corponation Will See You Now
creator: Benedikt Asare-Kowalczyk
description: A darkly comic corporate-approved satirical novel following Mireille, a Tier 3 mid-level compliance officer at a fictional corponation called Hexis Solutions, as she discovers that her entire department exists solely to generate the appearance of ethical oversight with no actual function. The satire is sharp but carefully calibrated — the novel was published by Halvex Media's literary imprint and approved at every stage, which many readers consider either a testament to Asare-Kowalczyk's craft or a sign that the satire doesn't land where it should. It was a bestseller in 2219.
medium: neural feed (primary distribution); physical hardcover (premium edition, Tier 4 gift market)
cultural_impact: Became the most-discussed novel in Meridian 88 for approximately eight months, generating endless debate about whether corporate-approved satire is satire at all or simply a pressure-release valve, a debate Asare-Kowalczyk refuses to engage with publicly.
controversy: An anonymous essay, widely circulated on underground neural channels, claims to be by a former Halvex editor detailing the seventeen specific changes demanded before publication — each of which, the essay argues, transformed a genuinely dangerous novel into a harmless one. Halvex denies the essay's authenticity.
story_hooks: The anonymous essay is real, and the former editor who wrote it is now missing — the last person to see them was trying to reach the novel's author.

A chapter cut from the final manuscript — the seventeenth change — exists somewhere, and it apparently names a real corponation executive by a barely-disguised pseudonym in connection with something genuinely criminal.
Asare-Kowalczyk has been approached to write a sequel under very specific contractual constraints; they are looking for someone to help them find a way to make it honest anyway.
